text:
lia moreno: Hi all — newbie trying to get the backend running. I did `docker compose up` but my service keeps timing out connecting to postgres:5432. Error in logs: "dial tcp 127.0.0.1:5432: connect: connection refused". I'm following the README.

lia moreno: compose.yml (excerpt):
```yaml
services:
  web:
    build: .
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:pass@postgres:5432/app_dev
  postgres:
    image: postgres:13-alpine
    volumes:
      - ./tmp/pg:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```

diego rios: welcome! quick checks: are you running web inside the container or on host? The 127.0.0.1 in the error suggests the app is trying localhost. If you're running `docker compose up` both services should be on the same network and `postgres` should be resolvable by name.

lia moreno: I'm running the web container via `docker compose up --build web` and tailing logs. I thought that would start the db too.

diego rios: when you pass a service name to `docker compose up` it only starts that service and dependencies declared with `depends_on`. If postgres isn't a dependency of web in the compose file, it won't start. Also profiles can opt you out if used. Check `docker compose ps` to see which containers are running.

lia moreno: ah! I had a separate profile called `dev` on postgres: `profiles: ["dev-db"]` and I was running `docker compose up web`. So postgres never started. rookie mistake.

diego rios: yep. either run both services (`docker compose up --profile dev-db web`) or add `depends_on: - postgres` to web and avoid profile for local dev. Also consider adding a simple entrypoint wait script or `wait-for-it` so web retries until postgres accepts connections.

lia moreno: fixed. brought up both, DB initialized. One more question: my pg data dir on host ended up owned by root and now container chokes on permissions. Any safe way to reset?

diego rios: if it's only local dev, stop compose, rm the host dir `rm -rf tmp/pg` and let compose create a fresh volume. If you need to preserve data, chown the dir to 999:999 (postgres user in the container) or run `docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/tmp/pg:/data alpine chown -R 999:999 /data`.

oncall-bot: Dev tip: For Apple Silicon, prefer images tagged `*-alpine` or `postgres:13` (multi-arch). If you hit emulation, see https://redwood.internal/devenv/m1 for workarounds.

lia moreno: thanks everyone — up and running now. I'll update the onboarding notes about profiles and `docker compose up <service>` behavior. :sparkles:
